**Issue with the most Yerxa articles**

| Issue | Publication date | Number of Yerxa articles |
|-------|------------------|--------------------------|
| **Volume 10, Number 5** (November 2009) | November 2009 | 2 |

*Volume 10, Number 5* contains two pieces written (or interviewed) by Donald A. Yerxa – the most among all the 2009 issues of *Historically Speaking*.

---

### Articles by Donald A. Yerxa in Volume 10 Number 5

| Page range | Title |
|------------|-------|
| 8‑9 | **“An Interview with Ken Albala: History on the Plate – The Current State of Food History”** |
| 25‑27 | **“Why History Matters: An Interview with John Tosh”** |

These two items are the only pieces in the November 2009 issue that list Donald A. Yerxa as author (interviewer) or as the speaking author. The evidence comes from the Project MUSE issue‑specific page for *Historically Speaking* 10(5), which shows the two entries with Yerxa’s name:

* “An Interview with Ken Albala.” – pp. 8‑9. (see search result snippet for 19423)  
* “Why History Matters: An Interview with John Tosh.” – pp. 25‑27. (see same search result)

Because no other Yerxa‑authored pieces appear in this issue—and no other 2009 issue contains more than one such piece—the November 2009 issue is the one with the maximum number of Yerxa‑authored entries.

steps.text:
**Issue with the most Yerxa articles**

| Issue | Publication date | Number of Yerxa articles |
|-------|------------------|--------------------------|
| **Volume 10, Number 5** (November 2009) | November 2009 | 2 |

*Volume 10, Number 5* contains two pieces written (or interviewed) by Donald A. Yerxa – the most among all the 2009 issues of *Historically Speaking*.

---

### Articles by Donald A. Yerxa in Volume 10 Number 5

| Page range | Title |
|------------|-------|
| 8‑9 | **“An Interview with Ken Albala: History on the Plate – The Current State of Food History”** |
| 25‑27 | **“Why History Matters: An Interview with John Tosh”** |

These two items are the only pieces in the November 2009 issue that list Donald A. Yerxa as author (interviewer) or as the speaking author. The evidence comes from the Project MUSE issue‑specific page for *Historically Speaking* 10(5), which shows the two entries with Yerxa’s name:

* “An Interview with Ken Albala.” – pp. 8‑9. (see search result snippet for 19423)  
* “Why History Matters: An Interview with John Tosh.” – pp. 25‑27. (see same search result)

Because no other Yerxa‑authored pieces appear in this issue—and no other 2009 issue contains more than one such piece—the November 2009 issue is the one with the maximum number of Yerxa‑authored entries.
